routes.name: EU/EEA free movement and residence
routes.summary: EU nationals don't need a permit to live and work in Malta. EEA nationals can stay while working, self-employed, self-sufficient, studying or as family members.

other: Rights can be limited on public policy, security or health grounds, or if you become an unreasonable burden on social assistance.
Registration timelines and permanent residence rules were not confirmed on the pages read.

routes.name: Residence permits for non-EU nationals
routes.summary: Identita's Expatriates Unit issues employment-related and non-employment-related residence permits to third-country nationals. Details, fees and conditions were not readable on the pages opened.

other: Check Identita's Employment Related and Non-Employment Related permit pages and the Expatriates Portal for conditions and fees.

routes.name: National Visa, Student Visa and Schengen Visa
routes.summary: Malta's Central Visa Unit handles Schengen, National and Student visas. Visa-free lists, transit rules and fees were not confirmed on the page opened.

other: Check the Central Visa Unit pages for who needs a visa and the current fee table.

sources.label: Identita: Central Visa Unit fees and applications

routes.name: Residency Malta programmes (MPRP, Nomad Residence Permit, Startup Residence)
routes.summary: Residency Malta lists the Malta Permanent Residence Programme, the Nomad Residence Permit, the Malta Startup Residence Programme and a Family Office Residency. Requirements and fees were not readable, so none are stated here.

other: Contact Residency Malta for requirements and fees. Thresholds and fees were not confirmed.

routes.name: Maltese citizenship (birth, registration, naturalisation, merit)
routes.summary: The Citizenship Agency lists routes by birth, registration, naturalisation (including long-term residence), exceptional services by merit and by direct investment. Residence years, language rules and the July 2025 amendments were not confirmed.

other: Residence years, tests and fees were not confirmed on the pages read.
The site has a separate dual or multiple citizenship section that was not readable.
